skill.name: cpp-pro
skill.description: Write idiomatic C++ code with modern features, RAII, smart pointers, and STL algorithms. Handles templates, move semantics, and performance optimization. Use PROACTIVELY for C++ refactoring, memory safety, or complex C++ patterns.
skill.summary: Guides modern C++ design, refactoring, testing, and performance work with RAII, templates, STL, and benchmarks.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Modern C++ projects need careful design to avoid memory, concurrency, and performance defects. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward idiomatic C++ implementation and review.
actual_capabilities: Guides idiomatic C++11 through C++23 design and implementation.
Applies RAII, smart pointers, const correctness, and exception safety.
Supports templates, concepts, move semantics, and perfect forwarding.
Recommends STL algorithms, containers, and concurrency patterns.
Plans CMake builds, unit tests, sanitizer checks, and benchmarks.
limitations: Does not run compilers, tests, sanitizers, or profilers by itself.
Requires project context to choose standards, libraries, and tradeoffs.
Cannot guarantee performance improvements without measured benchmarks.
Does not replace expert review for safety-critical C++ systems.

use_cases.title: Modernize legacy C++
use_cases.description: Replace manual ownership with RAII, smart pointers, and clearer interfaces.

use_cases.title: Review performance-sensitive code
use_cases.description: Identify allocation, copying, threading, and algorithm choices that need measurement.

use_cases.title: Design reusable templates
use_cases.description: Plan concepts, forwarding, compile-time checks, and documentation for generic interfaces.

prompt_templates.title: Review a C++ file
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this C++ file for RAII, ownership, const correctness, and exception safety. Summarize the highest priority fixes first.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one source file.

prompt_templates.title: Modernize a component
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this component toward modern C++. Use smart pointers only where ownership requires them. Preserve behavior and list test cases.

prompt_templates.title: Design a template API
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a C++20 template API for this requirement. Include concepts, error behavior, ownership rules, and documentation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize measured hot paths
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these benchmark results and source excerpts. Propose C++ performance changes, validation steps, and risks for each change.

output_examples.input: Review a class that manually deletes heap objects.
output_examples.output: The response identifies ownership risks, recommends RAII containers or smart pointers, and lists focused regression tests.

output_examples.input: Improve a template function with unclear compile errors.
output_examples.output: The response proposes concepts, clearer constraints, better diagnostics, and documentation for accepted types.

output_examples.input: Plan validation for a threading refactor.
output_examples.output: The response lists race risks, sanitizer checks, unit tests, benchmark comparisons, and rollback criteria.

best_practices: Provide compiler version, C++ standard, platform, and build system context.
Share failing tests, sanitizer output, benchmarks, or profiler data when available.
Ask for explicit tradeoffs between clarity, safety, compatibility, and performance.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for performance changes without a baseline measurement.
Do not hide ownership rules or lifetime constraints from the prompt.
Do not apply template metaprogramming when a simple interface is enough.

faq.question: Which C++ standards does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers modern C++ from C++11 through C++23, including concepts and move semantics.

faq.question: Can it create tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan or draft tests for Google Test, Catch2, sanitizers, and benchmark validation.

faq.question: Does it execute C++ code?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides guidance and generated content. Tool execution depends on the host assistant environment.

faq.question: Is it useful for legacy code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest staged refactors that improve ownership, safety, and readability.

faq.question: Can it optimize performance?
faq.answer: Yes, when given measurements. It should pair optimization advice with validation steps.

faq.question: Does it replace a C++ expert review?
faq.answer: No. It helps prepare and review work, but critical systems still need expert human review.
